chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'at al-Nakhas, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), saying to him, 'Is it permissible for me to buy the absconded slave girl from the people, give them the price, and seek her myself?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Buying her is not permissible unless you buy from them something along with her, a garment or goods, so you should say to them,

key_terms.الْآبِقَة: Absconded slave (one who has run away from their master)
key_terms.الْمَتَاع: Goods/property (used here to bundle the transaction)

ai.seo_question: How to legally buy an absconded slave girl according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) provides a practical legal solution (*hila*) to avoid *gharar* (uncertainty) or specific prohibition in purchasing an 'absconded' slave girl by bundling her with another item. This method ensures the transaction is valid by attaching the purchase of the fugitive to a distinct, known commodity, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity in commercial contracts. The ruling highlights the flexibility of fiqh in adapting to social realities while maintaining legal integrity.
